author: GamingBolt
description:
Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a difficult game to sum up, because even if you can categorize it as “dumb fun” - and I had more than my fair share across the campaigns and in Horde – it devolves into feeling so mundane, and rote, as to actually have me questioning my existence when unloading on Synths and wondering why we don't just nuke all these factions from orbit, forever, just to be sure. Even if you're a fan of the original, despite addressing the original's shortcomings, it doesn't feel like a meaningful evolution, much less a compelling Aliens story.

Perhaps the best way to describe it is through one encounter where I cut through a door, and it opened to reveal a Xenomorph standing tall. For several painfully long seconds, non reactive, even as the entire team proceeded to light it up until it seemingly got into character. And as someone who remembers the sheer terror it inspired while playing Aliens Versus Predator in 1999, that really says it all.
title: Aliens Fireteam Elite 2 Review - The Final Verdict

author: GamingBolt
description:
Onimusha: Way of the Sword's approach to exploration sticks to what the originals offered while expanding on them in exciting ways. Do I expect Kuchisake-onna to pop up and fight with massive scissors? No, but incorporating folktale figures like Shuten-dōji means we could see more than a few Kyoto-specific entities making their presence known (and putting up a fair challenge). 

Onimusha: Way of the Sword launches on September 4th for Xbox Series X/S, PS5, PC, and Nintendo Switch 2. As much as its combat, presentation values and Toshiro Mifune's likeness have stood out, I feel like the development team is hiding a secret ace of sorts with the exploration. Thankfully, we won't have to wait long to see how bizarre Musashi's adventure really turns out.
title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword's Approach to Exploration Could Be Its Secret Weapon

author: GamingBolt
description:
GTA 6 has finally stepped into the spotlight, and it’s been a thrilling time since we got a good look at what’s waiting for us in Leonida. We are sure the game will keep us occupied for a good while, but we’re now wondering how much of that time will be spent admiring how incredible it all looks. There’s some serious graphical wizardry at play in Rockstar’s latest and potentially greatest title, and it’s very interesting to compare it to the last instalment in the franchise. 

It’s a perfect showcase of how far the studio has come over the years, and how much it has managed to improve on things it was already quite good at. Join us as we look at the evolution of a formula and art style that has withstood the test of time, and might even chart a course into the future for the rest of the gaming world.
title: GTA 6 vs. GTA 5: A First Look at the Massive Graphical Upgrade - The Leap Is Bigger Than We Expected
